title: Social media sadness
paragraphs: Are you a social media addict? Are you always checking your smartphone to see how many 'likes' you've received for your latest post? Maybe you feel comforted by the notification sound that someone has sent you a message?

Don't worry, you're not alone. We check our phones an average of 150 times a day, and around 30% of the total time spent online is dedicated to social media. Some experts now fear this habit could be damaging our mental health.

This is something particularly afflicting young adults, according to a study from the University of Pittsburgh. It found the more they used social media, the more likely they are to be depressed. In tests, those people who checked social media frequently were 2.7 times more likely to be depressed compared to those who spent most of their time generally surfing the internet, who had just 1.7 times the risk. The study found that exposure to "highly idealised representations of peers on social media elicits feelings of envy and the distorted belief that others lead happier, more successful lives."

Some of us certainly feel sad when we're ignored on social media sites, or when we see someone else having a better time than us. But depression is a more serious condition and clinical psychologist, Abigail San, recently told the BBC that, "It's a real issue, and it's been getting significantly worse over the last 5-6 years. You can get so hooked that it takes you away from your real relationships." However, Abigail does admit that social media is more likely to exacerbate pre-existing issues than directly cause them.

Other research by Glasgow University found that teenagers are affected by the 24-hour demands of their social media accounts. It found that those with higher levels of emotional investment in social media, and who use it at night, were more likely to feel depressed and anxious.

Despite these warning signs, why do some of us continue to keep clicking? Well, I suppose we all want to be liked and we don't want to miss out on a conversation that's taking place online. But we need to know when to switch off our virtual online world and connect with the real world instead.

vocabulary.entry: notification [n.] /ˌnəʊtɪfɪˈkeɪʃən/ 通知；通知消息

vocabulary.translation: 我收到了航班延误的通知。

vocabulary.translation: 这个网站致力于帮助学习者。

vocabulary.entry: afflict [v.] /əˈflɪkt/ 折磨；使痛苦 (书面语)

vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病折磨着数百万人。

vocabulary.entry: depressed [adj.] /dɪˈprest/ 抑郁的；沮丧的
vocabulary.example: He felt depressed after losing his job.
vocabulary.translation: 失业后他感到沮丧。

vocabulary.translation: 这本杂志展示了理想化的美丽形象。

vocabulary.entry: elicit [v.] /ɪˈlɪsɪt/ 引出；引起 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The joke elicited laughter from the audience.
vocabulary.translation: 这个笑话引起了观众的笑声。

vocabulary.entry: distorted [adj.] /dɪˈstɔːtɪd/ 扭曲的；失真的
vocabulary.example: The mirror gave a distorted reflection.
vocabulary.translation: 镜子产生了扭曲的映像。

vocabulary.entry: hooked [adj.] /hʊkt/ 上瘾的；着迷的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: She is hooked on reality TV shows.
vocabulary.translation: 她对真人秀节目上瘾了。

vocabulary.example: Stress can exacerbate health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 压力会加剧健康问题。

vocabulary.entry: anxious [adj.] /ˈæŋkʃəs/ 焦虑的；担忧的
vocabulary.example: She felt anxious before the exam.
vocabulary.translation: 考试前她感到焦虑。

vocabulary.entry: keep clicking [phr.] /kiːp ˈklɪkɪŋ/ 不停地点击 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He kept clicking the mouse, waiting for the page to load.
vocabulary.translation: 他不停地点击鼠标，等待页面加载。

vocabulary.entry: miss out on [phr.] /mɪs aʊt ɒn/ 错过；错失 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Don't miss out on this opportunity.
vocabulary.translation: 不要错过这个机会。

vocabulary.example: It's hard to switch off from work at home.
vocabulary.translation: 在家很难不想工作的事。

vocabulary.translation: 他每天花几个小时上网浏览。

vocabulary.entry: take away from [phr.] /teɪk əˈweɪ frɒm/ 使离开；减少 (固定搭配)

vocabulary.translation: 看电视占用了阅读时间。
